Between blinds, spend money in the shop to improve the run. Jokers change scoring and other effects; planet cards improve hand levels. Inspect an item's description and price before buying. Deck choice and unlocked stakes change later runs. This game is beta; its server setting controls whether it is available.

Select cards to form a poker hand, then play them to score chips multiplied by mult. Discard to replace selected cards. Hands and discards are limited, so reach the blind's target before your hands run out. Read each blind's rule before committing: boss effects can change what works.

Hit takes a card. Stand keeps your total. With two cards and enough chips, Double adds a matching bet, takes one card, then stands. Split separates two cards of the same rank into two hands with matching bets. You can split once. Each resulting hand plays separately. Disabled controls explain why an action is unavailable.

Going over 21 is a bust and loses the bet. A winning ordinary hand pays even money; a natural blackjack pays 3:2. A push returns your bet. Example: a winning 10-chip ordinary bet returns 20 chips in total, including the original 10. The shared card-room bankroll remains with your character when records are enabled.

Choose a bet, then deal when every seated player has bet or chosen to sit out. Each hand plays against the dealer. Get closer to 21 than the dealer without going over. Number cards use their number; face cards are 10. An Ace counts as 11 when that fits, otherwise 1. The dealer stands on 17, including soft 17.

Select a counter, then a highlighted diagonal square. Ordinary counters move toward the far edge. To capture, jump over an opposing counter into the empty square beyond it. If a capture is available, a jump is required. Continue with the same counter when another jump is available.

Reach the far edge to become a king. Kings can move and jump in both directions. Win when the opponent has no counters or no legal move. The two sides use blue and red counters. Add a bot for a solo game.

Check means your king is attacked: the next move must remove the check. Checkmate means the king is in check with no legal reply, and loses. Stalemate means the player to move has no legal move but is not in check, and draws. Add a bot to play alone. Resign concedes the game; a draw offer needs the opponent's agreement.

Select your piece, then a legal highlighted square. Rooks move along ranks or files. Bishops move diagonally. Queens do both. These pieces cannot jump over others. Knights move two squares in one direction and one across, and can jump. Kings move one square and cannot enter an attacked square.

Pawns move one square forward into an empty square, or two from their starting square if both are clear. They capture one square diagonally forward. A pawn on the far rank promotes. En passant captures a pawn immediately after its two-square advance. Castling moves the king and rook together; neither may have moved, and the king cannot castle out of, through, or into check.

Choose a column to drop one counter into its lowest empty space. Players alternate turns. Connect four of your counters horizontally, vertically, or diagonally to win. A full column cannot accept another counter. A full board with no winner is a draw. Add a bot to play alone.

Subtract each score from your remaining total. Win by reaching exactly zero with a double; the centre bull counts as a double. Going below zero, leaving one, or reaching zero without a double busts the turn and restores its starting score. Example: with 40 left, double 20 wins. Your character's condition can affect accuracy.

Each player starts at 501. Flick upward on the board to throw. For a keyboard throw, focus the board, choose the target, then use the throw control. Each turn has three darts. A single scores the number, the narrow outer ring scores double, and the inner ring scores triple. The outer bull is 25; the centre bull is 50.

Check passes without adding chips when nothing is owed. Call matches the current bet. Raise increases it. Fold gives up this hand and chips already committed. All-in commits your remaining stack. Side pots keep a short stack eligible only for the chips it has matched. Blinds are forced opening bets based on the table stake.

If the current bet is 10 and you have already put in 4 this betting round, calling adds 6. A raise makes the total to match larger; the action control shows its amount. Chips committed in earlier rounds are already in the pot. Read the amount before confirming an action. Cashing out through Leave returns the chips still in your stack.

Straight flush: five consecutive cards of one suit. Four of a kind. Full house: three of one rank and two of another. Flush: five of one suit. Straight: five consecutive ranks. Three of a kind. Two pair. One pair. High card. A royal flush is the highest straight flush. An Ace can be low in A-2-3-4-5. Equal categories compare their ranks and remaining kickers; equal hands split the pot.

Buy in and seat at least two players, including bots if wanted. Each player gets two private cards. Five shared cards appear in stages: three on the flop, one on the turn, one on the river. Your best five-card hand can use any combination of your cards and the shared cards. Win at showdown, or make every opponent fold.

Right-drag on the felt to aim. Use the wheel for power, then click or press Space to shoot. Arrow keys adjust aim and power. Ctrl + wheel changes spin. With ball in hand, choose a clear spot for the cue ball before shooting.

In 8-Ball, clear your group, then pocket the 8-ball legally. In 9-Ball, hit the lowest numbered ball first; legally pocketing the 9 wins. The rules chip names the active rules. Standard 8-Ball requires a called ball and pocket. Casual 8-Ball removes ordinary called shots. A scratch is a foul. Read the table's foul message before the next shot.

Move cards between columns in descending order with alternating red and black suits. A valid sequence can move together. Only a king can fill an empty column. Build the four suit foundations from Ace to King. Drag a card, or select it and then select a highlighted destination.

Select the face-down stock to draw. Only the top waste card is available. The draw-one or draw-three setting controls each draw; the stock can cycle. Undo reverses a move. New Deal replaces the current game and asks before discarding unfinished play.
Reading does not pause the table or its turn clock.

Green means the letter is in the correct position. Yellow means the letter is elsewhere. Grey means that copy of the letter is not needed. Repeated letters are counted: if a guess has two copies and only one is marked, do not assume the answer contains both.

Enter a five-letter word with the keyboard or letter buttons, then submit it. You have six accepted guesses. An incomplete guess or a word outside the accepted list does not use a row. Backspace removes the last letter before submission.
